subject: Inference cost pressure: discovery recap & next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Emily Johnson <emily.johnson@clarityai.com>, Arjun Mehta <arjun@clarityai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inference cost pressure: discovery recap & next steps

Hi Emily / Arjun —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so everyone has the same context. I pulled the key points we discussed and outlined proposed next steps below.

Pain points (what you told us)
- Unit cost is the dominant blocker for broader LLM use: benchmarking shows ~3–4x higher token cost than product can sustain.
- Workload patterns: mix of short transactional prompts (avg 40 tokens) and periodic long-context classification runs (avg 8k tokens).
- Current stack: in-house endpoints on GCP with A100s, custom batching but no global KV caching, limited GPU utilization (40–55%).
- Procurement: procurement window in Q2; budget requires a credible 25–40% reduction in per-user inference spend to proceed.

Success criteria you shared
- 2x–3x reduction in per-token spend for production traffic (baseline = current spend).
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 350ms for transactional prompts.
- No drop in qualitative output for core ranking / NER tasks.

Openness / constraints
- Highly open to model quantization and 4-bit paths if we can validate output parity.
- Willing to try caching for repeated prefixes but need guidance on data retention & privacy.

Redwood hypotheses (how we can help)
- Intelligent batching + adaptive KV prefix caching could reduce token compute by 30–50% for transactional flows.
- Quantized model variants (8-bit / 4-bit) + tuned kernels should give 1.8x–2.5x raw token compute savings depending on accuracy tolerance.
- Smart routing to cheaper GPU tiers for background long-context jobs while keeping transactional traffic on lower-latency nodes.

Requested artifacts from you
1) The small anonymized sample traces you mentioned (10 min window + 1 week aggregate): request sent; you said you could export as CSV — thanks.
2) Any internal SLOs / latency budget doc (even informal).

Next steps (owners & timing)
- Emily / Arjun: share the sample traces and the procurement window by Wednesday 10 Mar.
- Aditya (cc’d): I’ve asked Aditya to produce a rapid cost hypothesis deck (quant & caching scenarios) by Thu 11 Mar. He'll also propose a short pilot footprint.
- Kimberly: I’ll schedule a 30-min technical design call next week to align on data sharing and privacy requirements.

Attachments: I asked for a short extract (clarity-inference-metrics.xlsx) during the call — paste it here when possible.

Thanks — appreciate the candid context. If I missed anything obvious, please flag.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Inference cost pressure: discovery recap & next steps

Kimberly / Ben —

Thanks — read Emily's reply. I sketched a rapid hypothesis and an experiment plan this morning (attached). High-level:
- Pilot scope: run two parallel routes for 2 weeks on a slice of traffic (5% of transactional requests):
  * Route A (safe): optimize batching + KV prefix cache on current FP16 model; measure end-to-end token reduction and p95 impact.
  * Route B (aggressive): serve quantized int8 (and experimental 4-bit on a shadow path) with identical prompts and run automatic QA checks.
- Expected near-term cost delta (rough):
  * Route A: 20–35% unit-cost reduction via batching + cache reuse (depends on prefix repeat rate).
  * Route B: 40–65% compute reduction at the kernel level; end-to-end savings closer to 30–50% once infra overheads included.
- Acceptance criteria: no more than 2% degradation on a small evaluation suite for critical tasks; p95 latency < 350ms for Route A and < 450ms for Route B (we'll throttle traffic if degraded).

I attached a short PDF with microbenchmarks (redwood-cost-hypothesis.pdf) and a checklist for required sample traces. If we get Emily's traces by Wed EOD we can stand up a minimal pilot by 16 Mar and provide a preliminary readout the week after.

Ben — can you sanity-check engineering effort (rough estimate) and whether we can allocate a single TPU/GPU pool for the shadow 4-bit experiments?

-Aditya

[attachment stub: redwood-cost-hypothesis.pdf (pdf, 420KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inference cost pressure: discovery recap & next steps

All — quick calibration from infra/ops side.

Summary answers:
- We can provision a 3-node GPU pool (mix of v100/A100 spare capacity) for a 2-week pilot; ops effort ~2 engineer-weeks to wire the routes and safe rollback.
- For caching: we'll need a small Redis cluster (2 nodes) to hold prefix KV with TTL control — ~1 engineer-week to integrate and test.
- Shadow 4-bit: we can run it as a nonblocking shadow on existing GPU pool; memory/pinning work should be done by our low-level runtime team — 1.5 engineer-weeks conservatively.

Impact estimate (very rough):
- If Aditya's numbers hold, a combined pilot (Route A + B) should demonstrate ~30–45% net unit-cost improvement for the targeted slice. That's likely to scale to 20–30% for full production considering variance in prefix repeat rate.

Next tactical steps (owner / date):
- Emily / ClarityAI: upload traces to Drive by 2027-03-10 EOD (Kimberly will confirm).
- Aditya: pilot config + runbook by 2027-03-11 (in HubSpot link).
- Ops (Ben): provision GPU pool and Redis test cluster by 2027-03-14.
- Kimberly: book the technical kickoff (30m) for 2027-03-15.

I’ll follow up in HubSpot with a short checklist and the infra ticket.
